clauses.text:
By virtue of the authority vested in 
me by section 303 of the Independent 
Offices Appropriation Act, 1950 (Public 
Law 266, 81st Congress), and as Presi­
dent of the United States, section 1  (d) 
of Executive Order No. 10011 of October 
22, 1948, authorizing the Secretary of 
State to exercise certain powers of the 
President with respect to the granting 
of allowances and allotments to Govern­
ment personnel on foreign duty, is here­
by amended to read as follows:
“(d) The authority vested in the 
President by section 303 of the Independ­
ent Offices Appropriation Act, 1950 
(Public Law 266, 81st Congress), and by 
section 302 of the United States Infor­
mation and Educational Exchange Act 
of 1948 (Public Law 402, 80th Congress) 
to prescribe, with respect to civilian offi­
cers and employees of the Government, 
regulations governing living-quarters al­
lowances, cost-of-living allowances, and 
representation allowances in accordance 
with, or similar to, such allowances au­
thorized by the said act of June 26,1930, 
or the said section 901 of the Foreign 
Service Act of 1946.”
This order shall become effective as 
of August 24, 1849.

status_research.rationale: I read the complete held EO 10085 original (14 FR 6617): a single paragraph rewriting section 1(d) of EO 10011 (Secretary of State powers over foreign-duty allowances), effective as of August 24, 1949. I read EO 10187, 10313 and 10391 (each restates section 1(d) of EO 10011 'as amended' in full with a new appropriation-act citation, so the 10085 wording of 1(d) is replaced in turn) and the held EO 10903 text (section 5(a) item 3: 'Executive Order No. 10085 of October 28, 1949' is hereby revoked, subject to section 5(b)). Section 5(b) preserves existing rules and regulations prescribed under the revoked provisions and actions taken under them until superseded; it is a savings clause for acts under the orders, not an independent continuing command of EO 10085, so it does not keep the order itself operative. The decisive source is the express named revocation in EO 10903; the restatement by EO 10187 is a further indication that the 10085 text of 1(d) ceased to operate earlier. I did not rely on the catalog note 'Revoked by: EO 10903' or the 1989 snapshot, which are editorial and agree. Effective date of revocation and any earlier ending remain lifecycle gaps; the gap on EO 10903 'target provision not located' is a machine matching gap only, since I read the revoking text in the held file. Provisional NO hypothesis only.
